assets.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: sharp high-resolution luxury fragrance collection still-life photograph for a website, 3:2 landscape composition. Deliver a high-resolution master, preferably 3840 x 2560 pixels.
Input image 1 is the existing collection photograph to REDESIGN; input images 2, 3, 4 are authoritative identity references for AMBER HOUR, OPEN SKY and IRON CROWN. They are contact sheets: use only the upper large front-view bottle from each.
Create a new tighter, more beautifully composed studio still life of exactly these three After Bells perfume bottles, front-facing, all entire caps and glass bases visible. Replace the generic arch and pale travertine lineup with a simple real dark-stone studio set: one broad low honed dark limestone block and a slightly lower adjoining slab, against a smooth warm charcoal backdrop. Arrange Amber Hour on the left slightly back, Open Sky in the centre slightly forward on the lower slab, Iron Crown at the right. All three bottles have the same real physical dimensions. Keep the group balanced with small clear gaps, occupying roughly 80 percent of the picture width and 74 percent of its height. No bottle overlaps another's label.
SHARPNESS: this is a commercial product photograph with the whole product plane in sharp focus, focus-stacked 100 mm macro lens at f/11 character. Perfectly legible label ink, clean but natural edges, detailed gold cap engraving, optical glass contours and fine stone texture. No bokeh or blur across any part of a bottle. No haze, smoke, bloom, lens flare, extreme caustics, artificial depth-of-field or painterly texture. Restrained photographic contrast and very controlled highlights, no oversharpening halos or CGI shine.
Preserve the reference bottle model precisely: clear thick faceted rectangular glass, bevelled shoulders, heavy clear base, short gold collar, ornate SQUARE GOLD CAP with the same symmetrical relief filigree motif. Amber Hour liquid rich amber; Open Sky pale green-gold; Iron Crown warm muted brown-amber. Retain the earlier small gold flakes mostly at the base; do not enlarge them.
Front labels: the original square thin satin-gold plaque with fine double dark border, serif black uppercase wordmark "AFTER BELLS", small line-diamond-line separator, then respectively clean black uppercase "AMBER HOUR", "OPEN SKY", "IRON CROWN". Accurate spacing and consistent label size across the three. Fine physical plaque edges, attached flush to glass. No sticker, text or plaque on any narrow side.
Lighting: large diffused softbox upper-left, weak front bounce for crisp readable label ink, narrow controlled edge reflections, gentle rear light through the liquid, natural grounded contact shadows. Fine subdued satin gold highlights with retained engraving detail. Bottle material is glass, not chrome; metal is gold, not luminous yellow plastic. Dark brown stone with modest natural variation and subtle shadow, no decorative additional props. Product tonal values clearer and brighter than background.
A single polished, realistic perfumery still-life photograph, no grid, no external lettering, no overlay captions, no watermark, no boxes, no extra bottles. Leave 10 percent breathing room at image edges.
assets.note: Website display width capped at 720 CSS pixels; source remains at its native resolution.

assets.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: a dedicated photographic background behind an elegant perfume-house newsletter invitation, landscape 3:2.
Create a real editorial still-life photograph of dark espresso-brown silk draped in broad gentle folds over honed brown-black stone. Place the silk folds mainly along the outer LEFT and RIGHT thirds, with one quiet diagonal fold near the bottom left and tactile fine-grained stone visible near the lower right. Leave the central 55 percent spacious, consistently dark and calm so a framed invitation and white lettering will be readable over it.
Lighting: a soft warm grazing light from the upper right catches the silk's natural champagne-bronze sheen and the minute stone grain. Deep coffee-brown shadows, restrained gold-brown reflected light, subtle natural material variation. Enough tonal separation at the outer edges to see the photograph without distracting from the form. The silk is real textile with fine fibre detail and believable folds, not molten metal, plastic, abstract CGI liquid or shiny gold foil. The stone has only subtle natural veins, not exaggerated marble swirls.
A beautiful, quiet, luxurious material study photographed on a medium-format camera, crisp natural texture, controlled highlights, polished perfumery art direction. No artificial blur or bokeh; the central darkness is produced by lighting and negative space. No bottle, no peacock, no people, no flowers, no candles, no jewellery, no furniture, no props, no letters, no logos, no text, no borders, no watermark. One unified photograph without a collage or grid.
